title: Exercise Plan
description: A training plan that can be uploaded into the Exercise Tracker app. Exercises are referenced by name, so a plan can be written without knowing anything about the user's device. Any exercise that does not already exist is created on import.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this plan format. Always "1.0".

mode.description: static: the same workout repeated indefinitely; beating the prescribed weight at the prescribed reps raises the plan's baseline. periodized: a fixed program over a date range; beating the prescription is recorded as a personal record but NEVER changes the plan.

units.description: Units the numbers in this file are written in. Weights are kg (metric) or lb (imperial); distances are km or miles. Converted on import.

scheduleType.description: weekly: days are pinned to weekdays. sequential: days rotate in order.

durationWeeks.description: Program length. REQUIRED when mode is "periodized".

weekNumber.description: Which week this day belongs to. Periodized plans only.

block.description: A group of exercises performed together. A plain exercise is a block of kind "single" holding one exercise. `rounds` is what is usually called sets: 3 rounds of a single-exercise block is 3x8.

kind.description: Use "superset" or "circuit" when the block holds two or more exercises performed back to back.

rounds.description: How many times through the block.

restBetweenExercisesSeconds.description: Rest between exercises inside a superset. Usually 0.

restAfterRoundSeconds.description: Rest after completing a full round.

name.description: Matched case-insensitively against the user's catalog; created if absent. Prefer common names such as "Barbell Bench Press".

reps.description: Strength only. Target repetitions per round.

weight.description: Strength only. In kg or lb per the plan's `units`. With weightMode "baseline", this is the STARTING weight used until the user establishes a heavier one.

weightMode.description: absolute: always use `weight`. baseline: use the user's current baseline for this exercise at this rep count. baselinePlus: baseline + `weightOffset`. baselinePercent: `weightPercent`% of baseline. Baseline modes only progress in a static plan.

weightOffset.description: For weightMode "baselinePlus", in the plan's weight unit.

rpe.description: Strength only. Rate of perceived exertion.

activity.description: Cardio only. Determines which metrics the app prompts for.

distance.description: Cardio only. In km or miles per the plan's `units`.

targetPace.description: Cardio only. Per km or per mile per `units`, as m:ss, e.g. "5:30". Supplying any two of durationSeconds, distance and targetPace determines the third.

intervals.description: Cardio only. A structured workout — fartlek, interval repeats, tempo, pyramid — as an ordered list of segments. Each segment is one repeated work/recovery pair, so `6 × 400m hard with 200m jog` is a single entry with repeat 6. Stack a warm-up segment, the work, and a cool-down to describe a whole session. When intervals are present, the exercise's own durationSeconds/distance should be the TOTAL for the session.

repeat.description: How many times this work/recovery pair is performed. Use 1 for a one-off block such as a warm-up.

label.description: What to call this segment, e.g. "Warm-up", "400 m repeats", "Surges".

workSeconds.description: How long each rep of the hard part lasts. Give this, workDistance, or both.

workDistance.description: How far each rep of the hard part covers, in km or miles per the plan's `units`. A 400 m rep in a metric plan is 0.4.

workPace.description: Pace to hold during the hard part, as m:ss per km or per mile per `units`. Supplying any two of workSeconds, workDistance and workPace determines the third.

restSeconds.description: How long the recovery between reps lasts. Omit for a segment with no recovery, such as a tempo block.

recoveryDistance.description: How far the recovery covers, in the plan's distance unit.

recoveryPace.description: Pace for the recovery, as m:ss per the plan's distance unit.
